strings.name: Serena Williams
strings.role: Tennis player · Winner of 23 Grand Slam singles titles
strings.summary: Serena Williams has shaped women’s tennis with her powerful serve, aggressive baseline play and sustained competitiveness. From public courts in Compton, she reached the world stage, winning 23 Grand Slam singles titles and major doubles honors with her sister Venus. Her career includes returns from injury, Grand Slam finals after childbirth, and a return to professional doubles in 2026 after stepping away in 2022.
strings.coverageNote: Selected career milestones through September 2026. Her 2022 departure and 2026 doubles return follow reports from tournament organizations; live rankings are not provided.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Early training
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Trained with her parents and sister in Compton, then continued her development in Florida
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Main events
strings.facts.fact-03.value: Tennis singles, doubles and mixed doubles
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: 23 Grand Slam singles titles
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Reached 23 titles by winning the 2017 Australian Open, a major women’s singles record in the Open Era.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Career Golden Slams in singles and doubles
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Won all four Grand Slam tournaments and Olympic gold in both singles and doubles, demonstrating competitiveness across disciplines.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Returns to US Open doubles with her sister
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Teamed up again with Venus in women’s doubles at the US Open, losing in three sets in the opening round.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Returns to professional doubles
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Partnered with Victoria Mboko at Queen’s Club in London and won their first-round match.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Steps away from the professional tour
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Left the tour after a third-round US Open defeat; this period did not prove to be a permanent endpoint.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Wins her 23rd Grand Slam singles title
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Defeated her sister Venus in the Australian Open final while pregnant, later giving birth and returning to competition.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Holds all four Grand Slam titles for a second time
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Won consecutively from the 2014 US Open through Wimbledon 2015, again completing a non-calendar-year sweep.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Wins Olympic singles gold
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Won singles gold at the London Olympics and added doubles gold with her sister.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Completes the first “Serena Slam”
strings.timeline.event-07.text: After winning the Australian Open, held all four Grand Slam singles titles at once across 2002 and 2003.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Reaches world No. 1 for the first time
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Became the WTA singles world No. 1 aged 20, returning to the top ranking in several later periods.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Wins her first Grand Slam singles title
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Defeated Martina Hingis in the US Open final, beginning her Grand Slam singles title collection.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Enters her first professional qualifying event
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Entered qualifying for a professional tournament in Quebec City at 14, gradually moving into the tour system.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Saginaw
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Moved with her family to California after her birth and began practicing tennis with her sister as a young child.
